description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in a combined training set, displaying a total of 13 distinct categories. There is no separate legend or internal percentage labels; instead, each category is identified by an external text label and a corresponding percentage, connected to its respective slice by a thin grey line. The slices do not appear to be ordered by size, and none are visually emphasized through explosion or offset. Moving clockwise from the top right, the largest slice is NQ in blue at 31.3%, followed by a very thin, nearly indistinguishable slice for SCIFACT at 0.1%, ENTFA in yellow at 1.8%, FACTCC in green at 2.6%, ANLI in dark orange at 4.6%, and FEVER in teal at 16.1%. Continuing clockwise, MULTIFC is shown in light purple at 0.5%, MULTINLI in light red at 11.3%, PUBHEALTH in yellow at 0.5%, SCITAIL in light green at 1.2%, SNLI in light orange at 15.4%, VITAMINC in light blue at 13.0%, and finally XSUMHUL in pale grey-blue at 1.6%.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training set, comprising 13 slices. Each slice represents a specific data source with distinct labels, colors, and percentage values. The largest data source is NQ, accounting for approximately 31.3% of the dataset, followed by FEVER at 16.1%. SNLI and MULTINLI are the next largest contributors, with 15.4% and 11.3%, respectively. Notably, VITAMINC shows a steady decline in its contribution compared to previous years, now accounting for only 8.0% of the dataset. Additionally, SCIFACT and PUBHEALTH are among the smallest contributors, with SCIFACT slightly exceeding PUBHEALTH at 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each data source in the training set.
